description: Variables are defined for the data-based evaluation of investigations (e.g. studies). A variable is characterized by its data type (e.g. integer, string, date) and value range. The variable can be either quantitative or qualitative, i.e. the value range can take numerical or categorical values.

categories.description: A set of predefined categories that serve as possible values for the variable.

datatypeInPrimarySource.description: Datatype of the variable, as defined in the original primary source system.

datatypeStandardized.description: Standardized datatype of the variable, as defined in the controlled vocabulary.

description.description: A description of the variable. How the variable is defined in the primary source.

hadPrimarySource.description: A primary source for a topic refers to something produced by some agent with direct experience and knowledge about the topic, at the time of the topic's study, without benefit from hindsight. Because of the directness of primary sources, they 'speak for themselves' in ways that cannot be captured through the filter of secondary sources. As such, it is important for secondary sources to reference those primary sources from which they were derived, so that their reliability can be investigated. A primary source relation is a particular case of derivation of secondary materials from their primary sources. It is recognized that the determination of primary sources can be up to interpretation, and should be done according to conventions accepted within the application's domain ([PROV-O, 2013-04-30](http://www.w3.org/TR/2013/REC-prov-o-20130430/)).

identifier.description: An unambiguous reference to the resource within a given context. Persistent identifiers should be provided as HTTP URIs ([DCT, 2020-01-20](http://dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/2020-01-20/)).

identifierInPrimarySource.description: The identifier of the item used in the primary source.

propertyURL.description: A URI template used to define the RDF predicate associated with the values in the column, relative to each row. The propertyUrl may point to standard, controlled vocabularies, or ontologies that define the semantic meaning of the column.

resource.description: The resource that the variable is used in.

stableTargetId.description: The identifier of the merged item that this extracted item belongs to.

surveyInstrument.description: The survey instrument the variable derives from.

technicalName.description: A technical name given to the variable.

title.description: The human readable name given to the variable.

variableGroup.$comment: This property can be regarded as inverse property of csvw:column. While csvw:column points from the table to the column, mex:variableGroup points from the variable (column) to the variable group (table).
variableGroup.description: The variable group that the described variable is part of. Used to group variables together, depending on how they are structured in the primary source.

title: Extracted Variable
